Hanaa Is a Fully Custom Steel Yacht With an Unconventional Layout and Huge Sundeck
7 photos
Photo: Antonini Navi
Fully custom yachts represent the pinnacle of maritime luxury, offering clients the opportunity to develop a watercraft from a blank page and to create something that matches their vision of life at sea. Unlike production yachts, which are built using pre-designed plans, custom yachts are completely bespoke, with every aspect of the design, from the hull architecture to the amenities and interior finishes, designed to reflect how the owner wants to cruise and spend their time on board.
One of the shipyards that set out to offer yacht owners fully custom alternatives in an industry dominated by semi-custom designs is Antonini Navi. The renowned Italian shipyard is known for working with demanding clients who are used to the best things in life, and for pursuing luxury and innovation with each new vessel it designs. The latest project launched by the shipbuilder is Hanaa, a 31.2-meter (102-foot) superyacht that is set to be delivered to its owner in the spring of 2027.
Built with a steel hull and an aluminum superstructure, Hanna is a fully custom vessel based on Antonini’s Evo 31 motor yacht design and boasts naval architecture and exterior design by Hydro Tec and interiors by Milan-based studio Hot Lab. It was designed in close collaboration with the seasoned owners, who purposely sought the Antonini Navi shipyard in La Spezia for its experience.
The brief asked for an “attractive and modern” design with all the characteristics of an explorer yacht , such as long range, seaworthiness, and comfort for extended stays onboard. The yard delivered by creating a displacement motor yacht that spans four decks and offers spacious interior living quarters and generous outdoor areas, with an unconventional layout that enables a more informal way of living.
Photo: Antonini Navi For instance, instead of dedicating the main deck to a traditional formal salon and dining area, the owner wanted a large gathering space arranged around a central lounge that seamlessly flows into the aft cockpit and outdoor lounging spaces, creating an inviting environment for spending time with friends and family.
The forward area, which is typically occupied by the master suite in other yachts of this size, has been configured as a flexible, multifunctional space that can serve as an office, a meeting space, or a dining area, depending on the owners’ needs, and it also incorporates a private terrace. The result is an open, flexible deck that enables indoor-outdoor living.
The owner still benefits from sumptuous private quarters, but in this case, they are located on the upper deck, alongside the helm station. The master suite opens directly into a generous aft terrace, complete with a lounge, bar, and jacuzzi. This arrangement ensures the owner has plenty of privacy, keeping their suite separate from the four guest cabins, which are on the lower deck. Three cabins for crew are also located on the lower deck.
Another interesting choice in terms of interior layout is the location of the crew mess, which can be found on the main deck, with direct access to the galley for more streamlined daily operations.
Photo: Antonini Navi Penned by Hot Lab, the interiors have been designed in close collaboration with the owner and are described by the company as contemporary and welcoming, featuring organic shapes and natural materials.
Moving up to the sundeck, which spans over 78 square meters (839 square feet), we discover another welcoming living area, arranged with sunpads, al-fresco dining, and a barbeque. According to the yard, this is “one of the most spacious areas for socializing and relaxing in this category.”
The yacht also features a spacious engine room for easier maintenance and a side garage for a tender up to five meters (16 feet) long.
As for the exterior design, the team at Hydro Tec created a contemporary profile with clean lines, a bulbous bow, and long stretches of glazing intended to bring more natural light inside.
With a maximum beam of 7.5 meters (24.6 feet) and a full-load draught of 2.4 meters (8 feet), the yacht stays below the 300 GT mark, and according to the designers, the focus was on creating an efficient layout for comfortable extended stays within a more compact explorer profile.
Photo: Antonini Navi “With EVO 31, we wanted to break the mould and demonstrate that, even in this size category, we have the capabilities to build safe, modern, top-quality bespoke metal yachts, with interior and exterior liveability comparable to that of much larger vessels,” explained Antonini Navi.
“EVO 31 demonstrates that steel can be a viable alternative to fibreglass even for yachts of this size, representing a choice that offers strength, safety, the highest quality and great design freedom,” the team continued.
Hanaa is the second fully custom yacht built by the La Spezia-based shipyard, following the 33.5-meter (110-foot) Seamore 34 yacht Matilde 7, which was launched in July this year. Construction on this unit officially started with its keel-laying ceremony in January 2024, and its steel hull and aluminum superstructure are built to commercial construction standards, in accordance with MCA and Cayman Islands requirements.
Powered by two Caterpillar C18 engines rated at 533 Kw each, the custom yacht is expected to reach a maximum speed of 13 knots and a cruising speed of 12 knots, with a range of 4,000 nautical miles at ten knots.
